sentence: This project studies why a microbe tolerates a toxic solvent and builds a streamlined strain to make useful products.
This project studies small molecules made by soil bacteria that bind rare earth metals and how these molecules choose between metals.
This project builds a network of database experts that makes biological data easier to find and reuse.
This project studies how changing the levels of cholesterol and other lipids affects brain-cell survival.
This project studies how interacting particle systems that cooperate can find global minimizers of nonconvex optimization problems.
This project builds artificial intelligence tools that let people create and edit 3D shapes using language, images and simple selections.
This project studies how entanglement can make sensing and communication work better when there is noise.
This project builds a system that uses satellite observations and machine learning to follow where wildfire smoke travels.
This project builds a machine learning method that recommends chemical sequences for long chain-like molecules that self-assemble into desired structures.
This project develops sensors, materials and treatment systems that keep drinking water free of contaminants.
This project studies how reused and recycled feedstock changes the way metal melts and solidifies when a laser builds parts.
This project studies how embryos prevent and correct mistakes while they develop, using mathematical theory and a microscope.
This project studies how deep neural networks adapt to favorable structures in their input data without knowing that these structures exist.
This project builds models and control techniques that estimate and reduce degradation in fuel cells used in trucks and aircraft.
This project looks for entanglement between an ion and its departing electron when small molecules are ionized by squeezed quantum light.
This project builds numerical methods for poromechanics models that preserve physical laws such as mass conservation.
This project develops algebraic and combinatorial tools for studying symmetry and spaces in homotopy theory.
This project builds theory and computational tools that use vortex beams to image molecular structure and ultrafast chemical dynamics.
